title: Having Successful Work Terms
content_markdown:
A quick guide to a rewarding Co\-op experience\.

## Set Goals

At the beginning of the work term, discuss goals with your supervisor\. Ensure you understand what is expected of you and plan how you will meet these goals by the end of the term\.

## Communicate

Communication is always a key to a successful work term\. Don’t make assumptions and ask relevant questions\. Keep your supervisor in the loop of your work progress regularly and let your supervisor know if you encounter any problems\.

## Take Notes

Always keep a notebook and write down instructions given by your supervisor or important action items discussed in a meeting\. This shows that you are paying attention and that you have an organized way to avoid having your supervisor repeat their instructions to you\.

## Know Your Deadlines

Managing your time and learning how to prioritize are also essential attributes to a successful work term\. If you encounter issues meeting your deadline, communicate with your supervisor to find a solution together\. Don’t wait until the last minute to inform your supervisor that you can’t make a deadline\.

## Be Mindful of Co\-op Requirements

Find out what you need to submit as part of the [Co\-op Work Term requirement](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/students/requirements)\. The Co\-op office will send you a reminder in the beginning and near the end of the work term regarding the evaluation and work term assignment\.

## Tips for Working from Home

If on a remote or hybrid placement, please refer to these [CEWIL Tips for working from home](https://www.cewilcanada.ca/common/Uploaded%20files/Public%20Resources/COVID/FINALStudent_tips_for_working_at_home_-_CEWIL_Canada.pdf) for best practices\.

title: Featured Student: Melanie Law
content_markdown:
July 18, 2023

[Melanie Law](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/masthead_focal_point_sm/public/feature-images/2024-08/Melanie%20Law%201.jpg?h=73ff2e3a&itok=RXHGkYwo)

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/community/chronicles/melanie-law)

## What is your field of study and when did you graduate?

I pursued a dual degree with a Bachelor of Science in Microbiology and Immunology and a Master of Management\. I graduated from my Bachelors in May 2022 and my Masters in December 2022\.

## Why did you choose to enroll in co\-op?

I chose to enroll in co\-op, because I was very interested in gaining skills and hands on knowledge that I could not gain in the classroom\.  
  
I also wanted to try different types of work environments and discover which ones suited me and my goals the best\.

## Which positions did you work during co\-op?

Throughout my 18 months, I had the good fortune of working at a variety of different positions\.  
  
My first placement was as a research assistant at Ascension Sciences, then a data curator in the Pavlidis Lab at UBC and lastly as a junior developer at PanGenomic Health Corp\.

## Can you share your favourite experience while in co\-op?

As part of team bonding, one of the companies I worked with would regularly schedule team hikes through the mountains\. The views were beautiful and it was a great opportunity to get to know my co\-workers outside of the workplace\.

[Melanie Law](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Melanie%20Law%202%20Smaller.jpg)

## What did you feel most challenged by and how did you overcome it?

One of the achievements I had been most proud of was being able to apply my experience with data science and natural language processing to create a workflow in Python that scraped research articles and assessed how favourably the online community viewed them\.

As the member of my team who was most familiar with this process, this project was assigned to me\. At the time, I initially felt out of place, because my background was strongly rooted in wet lab work, as compared to my peers who all came from computationally heavy programs\.

However, my ability to find my niche and contribute to my team went to show that everyone had their own strengths to bring\.

## How do you feel co\-op helped your personal growth?

Co\-op helped me immensely in developing my soft and technical skills\.

I have become more confident in articulating my ideas and not being afraid to put myself out there and ask questions\.

I  also became a lot more confident in my research and programming skills, talents that I didn’t fully realize I had before\.

## Did you have any unexpected challenges during co\-op?

With each new position, there was always a lot of learning to do – and it’s completely normal for it to feel overwhelming\.

An unexpected challenge for me was learning how to use a new operating system, that I had never used before\. Doing so helped me become more self\-reliant in performing my own troubleshooting and finding my own answers\.

## Is there anything you wish you knew at the beginning – before you started co\-op?

The co\-op program has a lot of resources that students can take advantage of\.

There were so many interesting job postings that I didn’t realize I had the qualifications for – and they were dream positions\.

I was also able to identify which qualifications employers looked for in candidates\.

For those considering co\-op who are unsure, I highly recommend joining the program\.

## What advice would you offer future co\-op students?

When applying for different positions focus on why you want to join that team and why you are passionate about what they do\. Thinking through your motivation beforehand can really help you build a connection with recruiters during the interview\. Additionally, look at interesting postings that may be outside of your field, you just might be surprised about how capable you are and how many skills transfer between fields\.

## After graduation, where are you headed with your career?

My next main goal is to complete my Master of Management, which will allow me to have a background in the life sciences, computational sciences, and business\. I hope to apply this skill set to the field of medicine\. I am grateful that my diverse background is an asset that will help me pivot different directions and explore my passions\.

**Keep in touch with Melanie**: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/law-melanie/)

title: Featured Student: Andrea Enriquez
content_markdown:
January 30, 2024

[Andrea Enriquez](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/masthead_focal_point_sm/public/feature-images/2024-08/Andrea%20Enriquez%20Photo%209.jpg?h=7b980530&itok=bQLmB7Om)

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/community/chronicles/andrea-enriquez)

## What is your major when do you plan to graduate?

I’m majoring in Nutritional Sciences and planning to graduate in 2025\.

## Why did you choose to enroll in co\-op?

Being in co\-op was not part of my initial plan for my undergraduate experience\.

However, I wanted to gain work experience that would prepare me for life post\-graduation, as well as explore fields that I’m interested in\.

I also consulted other friends and students who were already in the co\-op program\. All of them had such cool opportunities that it made me want to try it out\.

## Which positions did you work during co\-op?

I’ve worked two positions for my co\-op terms\.

My first position was as a camp counsellor for a non\-profit organization, CTS \(Connect\. Teach\. Sustain\.\) Youth Society, who provides free outdoor education for kids aged 12 \-18\. As a camp counsellor, I planned the day camp activities and executed them as well\.

At my current position as a Clinical Research Assistant in the Department of Anesthesiology at St\. Paul’s Hospital, I’m involved in many ongoing studies including screening, recruitment, enrollment and data collection\.

These research studies are quite diverse, dealing with patients undergoing Cesarean delivery to patients with open\-heart surgeries\. The ongoing projects also vary from feasibility studies, qualitative studies and randomized\-controlled trials\.

## Do you mind sharing some of the most beneficial skills that you felt like you learned on your placement as a camp counsellor?

One of the most beneficial skills I learned as a camp counsellor is being adaptable to change\!

Although it was just a 4\-month term, there were lots of unexpected changes during my employment\. If you have ever worked with kids, you know that their uniqueness can create dynamic situations\. Therefore, adapting quickly by accepting change and problem\-solving has proven to be a really helpful skill that I learned both during the job and after my placement \- with other co\-op terms and my personal life\.

## Anesthesiology is a hugely complex and extremely important aspect of hospital work\! As a Land and Food Studies student, what connections between your academic learning and your on\-the\-job responsibilities in the hospital were you able to make? Would you be able to talk about any particular research that you worked on?

As a Land and Food Systems student, human health is the main topic of my academic studies, which covers a wide range of topics like: human nutrition, anatomy, biochemistry and the healthcare system\.

In my responsibilities as an anesthesiology research assistant, I often encounter these disciplines and it is very interesting to see them all interacting\. For instance, I'm involved in a few studies on cardiac surgery patients\. My responsibilities include screening the patients based on their health history, to ensure that they fit the studies' inclusion/exclusion criteria\. Therefore, I often look at their labs with their general chemistry, as well as social history, and the type of surgery they will be getting based on their disease\.

Learning about human health in my degree made onboarding with my responsibilities slightly easier when I was starting out\.

## Can you share your favourite experience while in co\-op?

My favourite experiences in co\-op are hanging out and having fun with my co\-workers\.

My co\-op experience would not have been as enjoyable without my amazing co\-workers\. Whether working on tasks together or spending time outside of work, I always found myself laughing as loud as I could and truly appreciating everyone’s presence\.

[Andrea Enriquez](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Andrea%20Enriquez%20Photo%202%20edited.jpg)

[Andrea Enriquez](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Andrea%20Enriquez%20Photo%204%20Edited.jpg)

## It seems like you made a lot of wonderful and fulfilling connections on your co\-op terms\. Can you tell me about a particular time with your colleagues and how it positively impacted you: personally, professionally or both?

During my co\-op terms, I met amazing people, with different interests, who pursued a variety of pathways\. This exposed me to many mindsets and perspectives, that I had never thought of before, both in my career aspirations and personal growth\.

Professionally, I always pictured a linear path \- from step 1, step 2 and all the way to step n\. This was how I thought I would reach my end goal\. However, from my colleagues, I learned that we are ever\-changing and so it's also okay to change our minds\. Although my current career path in medicine has not changed, this perspective helped me to feel less pressure about my next steps and focus on my present, rather than being anxious about the future\.

Furthermore, my colleagues' genuineness and kindness made such an impact personally that I'm now less afraid to ask for help, as they're always ready to show up when needed as members of a community\.

[Andrea Enriquez](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Andrea%20Enriquez%20Photo%207%20Edited.jpg)

## What was your best achievement in co\-op?

My best achievement in co\-op was taking a leap of faith and getting out of my comfort zone\.

Before my first term, I didn’t have much knowledge of outdoor education or tackling the big project of planning a whole program\. Sure, I liked being out in nature, but that was all I knew\! As I started my job as a camp counsellor, many experiences and job responsibilities were outside my comfort zone, as well as situations that I have never been in\.

I would say I’m quite proud of how I tackled these experiences and how I carried myself through\. By being out of my comfort zone, I grew a lot\.

## What did you feel most challenged by and how did you overcome it?

My first job search was challenging\.

I applied to jobs each week and successfully landed interviews\. The problem was that the job offers that I received were not my ideal position\.

As the first work term slowly approached, I still needed a placement\. I felt stressed, balancing all of the interviews and applications while studying for finals\. I knew I had to take the pressure off and stop being so hard on myself\. My solution was to become more open\-minded about considering different positions\. This mindset definitely opened a whole set of job opportunities that I wouldn’t have initially considered – resulting in my first placement\.

As it turns out, my job as a camp counsellor has been one of the most fun and fulfilling experiences in my life\.

## How do you feel co\-op helped your personal growth?

The people I met during my placements were beneficial to my personal growth\.

Talking to my co\-workers and supervisors about their personal stories and career pathways allowed me to reflect on my values and what I want for my future career\.

I am incredibly grateful for the wonderful colleagues that I got to know during these placements\. I learned a lot from each person who shared their diverse journey and this allowed me to learn about myself\. Their kindness and support both professionally and personally made my experiences in co\-op incredibly enjoyable and worthwhile\.

## How do you feel co\-op has helped your career?

During the job search, I wrote tons of cover letters and resumes\. I went to a dozen job interviews\. This experience was truly valuable, as I now know the competitive nature of job hunting and the qualities that employers look for\. It helped me to become more comfortable and confident in advocating for myself regarding my skills, experiences and values\.

Furthermore, as I’m interested in the healthcare profession, the relationships that I fostered with physicians and hospital staff helped me gain first\-hand experience in the field, as well as an awareness of job options and understanding of the industry\.

## What advice would you offer future co\-op students?

Don’t get discouraged by the job application process\!

There are so many jobs out there and you truly gain something out of every encounter and experience\. Be open\-minded and if there are positions that you might have set your heart on – there will be other ones\.

Co\-op is the time to learn what you like and don’t like\. So, even if you don’t end up fully enjoying a placement, it’s still time well spent as you’ve discovered something about yourself\.

[Andrea Enriquez](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Andrea%20Enriquez%20Photo%208%20Edited.jpg)

## What are you looking forward to after graduation?

Currently, I’m not entirely sure about my next venture after graduation, which is exactly what I’m looking forward to\!

My options are to apply to medical school, evaluate other work experiences or explore and travel\.

title: UBC Science Co-op Indigenous Student Employment Resources
content_markdown:
UBC Science Co\-op Indigenous students can find employment resources below, including employment and funding opportunities\.

Read about [The Reconciliation Pole](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-reconciliation-pole) pictured above, which is installed on the southern end of the UBC campus near the Forestry building\. [The Reconciliation Pole](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-reconciliation-pole) encourages everyone who comes across it to learn more about the history of Indian residential schools and to understand their role in reconciliation between Indigenous and non\-Indigenous Canadians\.

## Services for Indigenous Students through UBC Science Co\-op

### Please find current job opportunities below:

Whether you’re enrolled in UBC Science Co\-op or not, we can help you by providing assistance with preparing a resume, cover letter, and practice interviews in your job application process\. Our team is here to assist you\. Email our office \([science\.coop@ubc\.ca](mailto:science.coop@ubc.ca)\) to book an appointment with a Co\-op Coordinator\.

[Contact Co\-op Office](mailto:science.coop@ubc.ca)

## Job Opportunities

### BC Public Service Agency

The Indigenous Applicant Advisory Service is available to applicants that self\-identify as Indigenous \(First Nations, status or non\-status, Métis, or Inuit\) seeking to work or already employed in the BC Public Service\.

For advice and guidance on applying and/or preparing for an interview for this opportunity, Indigenous applicants can connect with the [Indigenous applicant advisor](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/careers-myhr/job-seekers/indigenous-applicant-advisory-service)\.

Apply to be an intern below\.

[BC Public Service Agency \- Indigenous Youth Internship Program](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/careers-myhr/job-seekers/internship-co-op-opportunities/iyip/apply)

### BGIS

BGIS is a global leader in the provision of facility management, project delivery, energy & sustainability, asset management, workplace advisory and real estate services\. With a combined team of over 8,000 globally, BGIS relentlessly focuses on delivering innovative service solutions that create value for its clients\. Their sustainable economic partnerships advance through inclusive supply chain practices, authentic community engagement and transparent business practices\.

View their virtual career fair below\.

[BGIS \- Indigenous Career Fair](https://careerfair.indigenous.link/bgis/)

### Canada Revenue Agency \- Indigenous Student Employment Program

The Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\) offers temporary employment throughout Canada to qualified Indigenous students through the CRA’s Indigenous Student Employment Program \(ISEP\)\.

Work with the CRA to grow your professional network, refine your skills and learn new ones, gain experience doing various duties, do meaningful and valuable work that matters to Canadians and join an inclusive community committed to your success\.

ISEP hires all year round\.

[Canada Revenue Agency \- Indigenous Student Employment Program](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/campaigns/about-canada-revenue-agency-cra/canada-revenue-agency-hiring.html)

### Cheakamus Centre

Cheakamus Centre is a centre of excellence for outdoor, environmental and Indigenous cultural education, and a welcoming place for learning, gathering and sharing in nature\. Established in 1969, Cheakamus Centre is an overnight environmental education facility located on 165 ha of ecological reserve near Squamish, BC\. The Centre is located on the traditional territories of the Chi'yakmesh people of Skwxwú7mesh \(Squamish\) Nation in the heart of the newly designated Átl’ka7tsem/Howe Sound UNESCO Biosphere Region\.

[Cheakamus Centre \- Job Opportunities](https://cheakamuscentre.ca/about-us/job-opportunities)

### First Nations Health Authority

The FNHA is a trailblazing organization filled with meaningful work and rich with transformative learning opportunities\. Here you will find a sense of direction and belonging, with those who share your drive to create change in the world and in yourself – for better\.

[First Nations Health Authority \- Work With Us](https://www.fnha.ca/about/work-with-us)[First Nations Health Authority \- Indigenous Student Program Info Sheet](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/FNHA-Indigenous-Student-Program-EOI-Annual-Deadlines.pdf)

### Indigenous Career Fair

The First Nations House of Learning, in partnership with UBC Career Centre, hosts an annual career fair at the Longhouse for Indigenous students and pending graduates looking to meet with prospective employers\.

Employers representing a variety of sectors offer insights into summer internship openings, discuss career opportunities, and shed light on their respective workplace cultures\.

[Indigenous Career Fair](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/indigenous-career-fair/)

### National Research Council of Canada \(NRC\)

Are you a First Nation, Métis, or Inuit person?  Do you want to gain valuable work experience in your field of study? Are you interested in working on leading\-edge projects of value to Canada? Are you looking for amazing learning opportunities in a creative and diverse environment?

The NRC Indigenous Student Employment Program provides students with practical career\-related experience in research and development, engineering, and technology, administration, library science, computer science, trades, business, technology advice services, finance, human resources, and other professions\. Students work in a challenging and intellectually stimulating environment, while having access to superior equipment, facilities and expertise\.

[National Research Council of Canada \(NRC\) \- Indigenous Student Employment Program](https://nrc.canada.ca/en/corporate/careers/indigenous-student-employment-program)

### Province of British Columbia \- Indigenous Youth Internship Program \(IYIP\) 

This is an opportunity like no other\! The program is designed to support Indigenous youth in developing their leadership skills through on\-the\-job experience, a strong peer network, supportive colleagues, dedicated program employees, and IYIP\-specific activities\.

[Province of British Columbia \- Indigenous Youth Internship Program \(IYIP\)](https://bcpublicservice.hua.hrsmart.com/hr/ats/Posting/view/119405)

## When did you graduate and in what field of study?

2019 and Computer Science\.

## Why did you choose to enroll in co\-op? 

To gain experience and familiarity with what I believe is the career path I want and to confirm that it really was what I expected\.

[Gina Bolognesi](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/44745022394_0ce77bd6e3_c.jpg)

## Which positions did you work during co\-op?

Software Engineer at Tasktop for eight months and then Machine Learning Research Intern at Honda Research Institute, Japan, for one year\.

## Can you share your favourite experience while in co\-op?

The most memorable experience for me was exploring Japan outside of working hours\. Among a great many things, I hiked Mt\. Fuji and joined martial arts groups; the latter was particularly valuable since I was able to attend regularly over a long period of time\.

## How do you feel co\-op helped your personal growth?

It was an opportunity to try different experiences and environments, to explore and to discover what I like and don’t\.

## Would you recommend co\-op in another city? Why?

If that’s something you’re interested in, definitely\! Co\-op provided me with the opportunity to live in Japan for a year, which allowed me to see a different country and do much more than I would have been able to as a tourist, while also working in my field\.

## How do you feel co\-op has helped your career?

It gave me a clearer picture of what I want for myself, what I like/dislike, what’s important to me, and what works for me\.

## What advice would you offer future co\-op students?

Do it\! Don’t worry about delaying your graduation; life isn’t on a schedule and you even get paid to learn\!

title: Featured Student: Carly Pistawka
content_markdown:
April 1, 2022

[Carly Pistawka](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/masthead_focal_point_sm/public/feature-images/2024-08/HeadshotCarlyPistawka.jpg?h=eb653418&itok=WuhySPsA)

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/community/chronicles/carly-pistawka)

## What is your field of study?

I am in my fourth year in the Honours in Biotechnology program\. It is a joint UBC and BCIT program, where you spend two of your five years in a lab\-intensive schedule at BCIT\. The Biotechnology program includes courses in: microbiology, chemistry, immunology, virology, pharmaceutical development, regulations, process systems, statistics, biochemistry, and animal cell biology\. Having experience and education at both BCIT and UBC provides both theoretical and practical learning for a small \(22 person\) cohort\.

[Carly Pistawka](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/painweek2021.jpg)

## Why did you choose to enroll in co\-op?

Co\-op is one of the reasons why I chose to enter the biotechnology program\. As part of the program, I have four co\-op terms, totaling to 16 months of co\-op experience\. When I entered first year and applied for a major, the co\-op programs were very appealing, because it gives the ability to try out jobs in the field and help inevitably determine what you are, \(and aren’t,\) interested in\.

## Which positions did you work during co\-op?

For my first co\-op term in 2020, I worked as a bioinformatics research assistant at the Silent Genomes Project Activity 2 through the BC Children's Hospital Research Institute\. I did a lot of coding, analysis, and pipeline development for the project remotely from home\. For my longer, 8\-month co\-op, I worked as a research assistant under Dr\. Caroline MacCallum, where I worked on creating tools for medical cannabis education, such as: Powerpoints, handouts, infographics, and workplace impairment guidance documents\. Through this, I was able to work on projects that intersected multiple fields of interest, such as medicine, science, research, politics, public health, patient advocacy, harm reduction, and social justice\.

## Can you share your favourite experience\(s\) while in co\-op?

One of my favourite co\-op experiences with Dr\. MacCallum, was going through the process of publishing an academic paper\. I learned a lot during the process, got to know my co\-authors, and it was very satisfying to see the final product after working for months on brainstorming, researching, editing, creating figures, and revisions\. I also got to present in Las Vegas at PAINWeek, one of the world’s largest pain research conferences, which was an amazing experience\.

## What advice would you offer to future co\-op students?

I would suggest that, if co\-op students have the opportunity to pursue multiple placements, they try something new\! Co\-op is a great way to be able to try something you may be interested in, but know very little about\. For my first co\-op term, I applied for a bioinformatics assistant position with limited knowledge on bioinformatics\. I ended up really enjoying the work and learned a lot that has been applicable to my classes and other co\-op positions\.

I also would advise future co\-op students to ask and listen about the experiences of the people they meet during co\-op, including your coworkers, supervisor, and their network\. It is a great way to get insight into the field if you are interested in it\.

## What are you looking forward to after graduation?

While I do love sitting in on lectures, I am excited to work for a few years after graduation before attending any more school\. I am planning on applying to the Masters in Genetic Counseling program at UBC after taking a year or two off of school\. Through my co\-op experiences, I have learned that I would like to pursue clinical work with patients\.

title: Work Term Requirements
content_markdown:
There are several requirements to meet for each work term\. As a student of the UBC Science Co\-op Programs, you are expected to:

1.  Honour your commitment to an employer by fulfilling the terms of employment to the best of your ability\.
2.  Respect the policies, procedures, confidentiality and proprietary information of your employers\. Assume that information is confidential unless informed otherwise\. Conform to all conditions and rules that apply to employees in the organization\.
3.  Keep the Co\-op Coordinator informed of any changes in your address, contact, and work term information\.
4.  Help arrange for a Co\-op Check\-In Meeting between you, your Co\-op Coordinator, and your supervisor during the work term, preferably conducted during the second or third month of the term\.
5.  Advise the employer and Coordinator of any concerns or problems that you have with your work term assignment or working environment\.
6.  Complete your work term assignment and all work term documents in SCOPE\. Please refer to the [**Work Term Assignment**](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/students/report "Work Term Assignment") section for detailed instructions\.
7.  Remind your supervisor to submit the Employer Evaluation online via SCOPE by the first Friday after the end the work term

## When do I need to complete the Work Term Documents?

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    **Document**

## Why do I have a Co\-op Check\-In Meeting?

A Co\-op Check\-In Meeting is an opportunity for your Coordinator to discuss your performance and the educational merit of your work placement mid\-way through the term with your supervisor and you\. A mid\-term review could be valuable feedback to understand mutual expectations\.

## How does my supervisor fill out the evaluation?

Your direct supervisor will receive an email from the Co\-op office with login instructions to SCOPE prior to the end of your 4\-month work term\.  They will log in to complete your performance evaluation online\.  Please contact the Co\-op office if an email has not been received by the middle of your 4th month\.

## What are work term assignments?

A report at the end of each 4\-month work term is required for all work terms except your 1st work term\.  There are different options available: technical report, oral presentation, poster presentation, progress report \(not applicable to computer science students\) and blog/ wiki, user manuals, patent applications \(computer science students\)\.  More details can be found in [**Work Term Assignment**](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/students/report "Work Term Assignment") section\.

## Who do I submit the Work Term Assignment to?

Submit your report to your supervisor and they will be responsible for evaluating your report\. The evaluation forms are available online in SCOPE and your supervisor will receive their login instructions via email prior to the end of the work term\.

## How do I receive a Pass standing for my work term?

To receive a Pass, all Co\-op work term documents must be submitted by the deadline, and you must receive a “satisfactory” or better grade on your employer evaluation and work term assignment\.

## When may a fail standing be issued for work terms?

-   A student is dismissed with just cause by the employer
-   A student quits the job without permission from the Co\-op Coordinator and the Co\-op employer
-   A student receives an unsatisfactory evaluation from the employer
-   A student receives an unsatisfactory grade on their report/assignment and failed to rewrite
-   A student does not submit the student evaluation form at the end of each Co\-op work term

title: Featured Student: Miranda Clark
content_markdown:
October 22, 2024

[Two Science Co\-op students sit at a booth about preventing pollution\.](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/masthead_focal_point_sm/public/feature-images/2024-10/Miranda%20Clark%20Co-op%20Photo%202%20Edited.jpg?h=7ee397a8&itok=RYGSeywf)

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/community/chronicles/miranda-clark)

## What is your field of study and when will you graduate?

I'm currently completing a degree in Environmental Science, with a specialization in sustainability\. I will graduate in December 2025\.

## Why did you choose to enroll in Co\-op?

As Environmental Science is such a broad field, I wanted to better understand which industries and working environments would allow me to make the most significant contributions to limiting the impacts of climate change and environmental degradation\. 

## Which positions did you work during Co\-op?

I held two eight\-month co\-op positions with Environment and Climate Change Canada \(ECCC\) during my Co\-op\. First, I worked in the compliance promotion program and secondly in the clean transportation directorate, specialized in marine transportation\. 

## Can you tell us about Environment and Climate Change Canada's \(ECCC\) Compliance Promotion Program?

ECCC's Compliance Promotion Program strives to ensure industries are complying with environmental regulations\. Specifically, we perform outreach to increase regulated communities awareness of regulations and their requirements, so we can strengthen environmental protection in Canada\. 

## Are you able to share any projects that you worked on? 

With my compliance promotion Co\-op role, I frequently prepared and sent out campaigns which often included fact sheets or other informative resources to remind large groups of stakeholders of their regulatory requirements\. I also prepared a large performance indicator project to analyze the impact of different types of engagement on regulatory compliance\.  

In my policy and research analyst role with the clean marine transportation team, I've worked on various research reports to help decarbonize marine transportation in Canada\. For these projects, I've written sections of reports and literature reviews as well as conducted research and statistical analysis of environmental or technical solutions for marine transportation climate initiatives\.  

## Can you share your favourite experience while in Co\-op?

I've really enjoyed the entirety of both of my Co\-ops so far\. 

I think that one of my favourite experiences was preparing the performance indicator project in my compliance promotion role, as this allowed me to use some of my academic research skills in a real world scenario and I could see that the results would be impactful on the work of Environment and Climate Change Canada\. 

## What was your best achievement in Co\-op?

One of my biggest achievements was receiving an award from my regional director for my volunteer efforts with the wellness and green team of ECCC\.   
  
I was very involved in organizing events and improving the community in my department and the award recognized these efforts and going 'above and beyond' my Co\-op student's duties\.   
  
While the recognition wasn't important, showing that my efforts were exceeding my job description made me proud at how hard I worked to succeed\. 

## What did you feel most challenged by and how did you overcome it?

When I started my job in clean marine transportation, I was shocked by the academic nature of the role\.    
  
However, by drawing on my scientific knowledge, I successfully performed the necessary tasks\. While initially this felt difficult, as it had been a while since I was in school, I worked hard, as well as reviewed assignments and notes, to best complete the tasks given to me\. 

## How do you feel Co\-op helped your personal growth?

Co\-op helped me grown significantly as a person\. I learned how to effectively prioritize tasks and develop professional relationships, with all sorts of people from different backgrounds with different skill sets\. 

[Image](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Miranda%20Clark%20Co-op%20Photo%201%20Edited.jpg)

## How do you feel Co\-op has helped your career?

It allowed me to scratch the surface of the environmental field\. 

I now understand far more about how the government works and which roles I could play within it to make significant impact to climate action\. 

I better understand some of the challenges involved in implementing large scale impacts and while this had led to feelings of frustration, I think that I can employ this knowledge to make a more meaningful contribution to change through my career\.  

## Which supports from the Co\-op program \(workshops, practice interviews, etc\.\) do you feel best supported you? Can you talk about the direct impact on your career? 

I found the practice interviews, as well as reviews of my resume and cover letter were very helpful to securing my jobs\. 

I did a mock interview a couple days before my first interview \(for my Environment and Climate Change Canada\) role and Sanya's feedback set me up for success in the real interview\. 

## What advice would you offer to future Co\-op students?

I think taking the opportunity to do as many different Co\-ops as you can is such a unique experience and incredibly valuable to kick start your career\. I also recommend consistently taking initiative within your Co\-op roles and ensuring you don't become complacent\. 

As a Co\-op student, I think it's easy to simply do the work that you are given and complete it successfully\. However, going above and beyond to learn new things and advocate for your career progression will make all the difference in the success of your Co\-op\. 

## What are you looking forward to after graduation?

I'm looking forward to jumping back into this field and beginning to make more of a difference in climate action\. 

I'm unsure if this will mean working at ECCC post graduation, or starting a masters in sustainable business in Europe, but I'm excited to see what happens\. 

My Co\-ops made me far more eager to dive in, develop my skills and seek new opportunities\. 

**Keep in touch with Miranda**: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/miranda-clark-7a7394259/?originalSubdomain=au), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/miranda.clark_/)

title: Featured Student: Peipei Zhong
content_markdown:
November 7, 2025

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/chronicles/Peipei-Zhong)

[A cartoon scientist in a lab surrounded by flasks with yellow liquid in them holds a beaker with yellow liquid in it\.](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Peipei%20Zhong%20Promotional%20Poster.jpg)

## What is your field of study and when will you graduate?

 I’m studying Biochemistry and expect to graduate in April 2026\.

## Why did you choose to enroll in Co\-op?

 As an international student without many local connections, I value having a reliable platform for work opportunities and professional guidance\. 

The Co\-op program provides both: not only does it connect me to meaningful placements, but it also offers support from coordinators and mentors\. For example, my Coordinator advised me on how to frame areas of growth during interviews by focusing on what I’m actively working to improve\. This kind of support has been invaluable\.

## Which positions did you work during Co\-op?

 I worked at Lallemand Inc\. as a bioprocessing intern and worked on application testing with bio\-ingredients in biotechnology\. 

This role served as a bridge between yeast extract R&D and product management\. I independently managed all aspects of the lab work for my supervisor, including literature review, protocol development, scaling calculations, scheduling, experimental design and execution and fundamental data analysis\.

## What was your best achievement in Co\-op?

One of my proudest achievements was authoring the department’s first Biotech Intern Manual \(24\-pages, 10,000\+ words\) and creating four educational videos about what my role mainly deals with\. 

Alongside these, I completed an independent project \(with report, poster and presentation\) and supported more than five auxiliary projects, to which I contributed precise, high\-quality data \(with an average standard deviation of just 0\.0005\)\.

Here are the educational video links: [https://youtube\.com/playlist?list\=PLkVmrXjuJE7gxXzW9inRLXs27CEv73nd\_&si\=eItzoI6SSfy5zGI7](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLkVmrXjuJE7gxXzW9inRLXs27CEv73nd_&si=eItzoI6SSfy5zGI7)

## What about the best day you had in your Co\-op city, Vancouver and beyond?

My best day was when our lab team gathered for a pool party at a supervisor’s house, where we shared both work and life experiences\. I found the conversations inspiring\. They gave me a clearer sense of how I could contribute more meaningfully during my internship\. For example, I later developed an intern scheduling Excel, inspired by other lab’s management approaches\.

## Can you share your favourite experience while in Co\-op?

My favourite experience was benchmarking through microplating, where I can compare the performance of different microbial strains across company products\. 

This not only gave me scientific insights into strain characteristics, but also broadened my understanding of the industry and business competition: how product performance links to specific components and what sets the best products apart\. It gave me the chance to apply what I’d learned, think creatively and see the impact of my work\.

## What did you feel most challenged by and how did you overcome it?

The challenges came in stages\. 

At the beginning of my internship there was no structured training protocol, so I created my own\. I documented my daily schedule and experimental steps, reflected on mistakes and refined my approach\. 

This process helped me connect scattered tasks into a clear, systematic overview of my role across projects\. Later, as I became more confident technically, the challenge shifted to deeper R&D tasks such as bioprocess optimization, including adjusting bacterial culture conditions to maximize specific metabolite outputs\. 

That transition from assessment\-style work to more research\-driven problem solving was very exciting\. This required integrating multiple skills: experimental design, literature review, rapid learning of new concepts and analytical tests, as well as drawing conclusions through statistical analysis and software tools\. Overcoming this stage taught me how to think like a researcher rather than just a technician\.

## Managing the balance between academics, Co\-op responsibilities and a personal life can be intense – what are your self\-care practices and/or how do you manage stress?

I create rest with a complete nighttime routine: taking a shower, doing skincare, wrapping myself in a scented quilt and watching stand\-up comedy\. 

This helps me relax and get consistent sleep, which keeps me energized for both work and study\.

## How do you feel Co\-op helped your personal growth?

Co\-op helped me grow by showing me that managing life is much like managing projects\. 

By using resources proactively and collaboratively, staying organized and building the right skills, I handled more responsibilities with confidence\. This gave me the chance to contribute to process improvements and increase my impact in meaningful ways\.

## How do you feel Co\-op has helped your career?

Co\-op shaped how I think about science, not only as discovery, but also in terms of customer needs, product optimization and real\-world impact\. 

Early in our careers, opportunities often come through skills and interviews, but over time they come from the trust we build and the impact we deliver\. Co\-op gave me the foundation to develop both\.

## Which support from the Co\-op program \(workshops, practice interviews, etc\.\) do you feel best supported you? Can you talk about the direct impact on your career and/or personal growth?

 All of the preparation resources, including workshops, practice interviews and question lists, were very helpful\. I’ve come to see that getting a Co\-op position is not the end, but rather the beginning of a larger journey\. 

What I value most is the sense of community: being able to connect with people from diverse fields who all share the same goal of supporting students in taking their first professional steps\. For example, the Co\-op podcast was especially meaningful to me, as it provided real stories and advice that helped me navigate challenges and stay motivated\. These experiences not only strengthened my skills but also gave me a stronger sense of direction and belonging as I prepare for my future career\.

## What advice would you offer to future Co\-op students?

Make reflection a habit\. 

Writing my work report and updating my CV was much easier, because I had kept daily, weekly and monthly notes on what I learned and accomplished\. 

Reflection not only makes reporting smoother, but also helps you track your growth and see how far you’ve come\.

## What are you looking forward to after graduation?

 I’m looking forward to graduate school, where I hope to build on my computational skills and integrate them with my biochemistry background to tackle practical human health challenges\.

title: Featured Student: Ching Zhang
content_markdown:
August 19, 2026

[Featured student: Ching Zhang](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/masthead_focal_point_sm/public/feature-images/2026-08/Copy%20of%20Co-op%20Chronicles%20-%20Ching%20Zhang%20%281%29.png?h=876d0211&itok=N-E8wkr5)

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/chronichles/Ching-Zhang)

### What is your field of study and when will you graduate/did you graduate?

I graduated from UBC in May 2026 with a Bachelor's of Science in Biology, with a minor in Oceanography\.

[UBC Science Oceanography graduate Ching Zhang](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Copy%20of%20Co-op%20Chronicles%20-%20Ching%20Zhang.png)

### What made you decide to enroll in Co\-op?

I actually wasn't planning on doing co\-op when I started my degree\. I enrolled in co\-op a bit later \- in the 3rd year cycle rather than 2nd year\. I was doing research for 2 years at that point with a few labs at UBC, thinking that I would stay in academia\. I heard positive feedback from lab mates and friends about what co\-op and industry was like, so I decided on a whim to try it out\.

### Which positions did you work while in the Co\-op program?

I worked as an In\-Vitro Assay Development Scientist at Xenon Pharmaceuticals in Burnaby for eight months, then spent my last six months as a Platform Biologist with the Encoded Technologies/Affinity Selections and Biophysics Group at GSK in Boston, Massachusetts\.

[Image](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/04%20edited.jpg)

### Can you share your favourite experience from your Co\-op placement\(s\)?

At my first co\-op with Xenon, it was cool to see how my existing skillsets were translated into high\-throughput solutions, and how they played a part in a bigger pipeline\. It was eye\-opening to see how science and corporate co\-existed with each other in a company format rather than a lab alone\. I think that some people would probably find corporate style meetings boring, but I actually enjoyed the balance it provided with lab work, and they gave me the opportunity to see the work other people were doing on the same project I was working on\.

At my second co\-op with GSK, I enjoyed how cross\-functional and collaborative the environment was\. I got to learn a lot of new techniques from other teams and coworkers because we all collaborated on projects\. I also appreciated that with working for a bigger biotech, I got to spend my time learning and working on a variety of projects and targets as opposed to a deep dive on just one\.

> I got to learn a lot of new techniques from other teams and coworkers because we all collaborated on projects\. I also appreciated that with working for a bigger biotech, I got to spend my time learning and working on a variety of projects and targets as opposed to a deep dive on just one\.

### What was your best achievement in Co\-op?

At both my co\-op placements, I worked on projects that directly contributed to company portfolio targets\. I think my best achievement was being able to summarize my impacts, work and contributions, and present these to my teams, including upper\-level management\. It was definitely a little anxiety\-inducing, and it was the first time I had to present \(and answer questions\) to a group that large \- about 50\+ people each time\. I think it's easy to have tunnel vision and imposter syndrome when you work on something for a long time, but receiving a lot of positive feedback after both presentations helped me realize that the work I did was important and would be carried forwards in the future\.

### What about the best day you had in your Co\-op city \(either in Vancouver or beyond\)?

At GSK, I had the opportunity to get involved with community outreach projects\. One of these was called "Science in Schools", an initiative to make science more accessible to high school students\. I got to spend the day with my coworkers at a college prep academy in Dorchester, MA, where we set up interactive activities for the students and introduced them to lab basics, such as micro pipetting, DNA work, and lab PPE\. It was very rewarding to see the students engage and have fun with the experiments we had set up\.

[Image](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/06%20edited.jpg)

### What was the most challenging prior or during your Co\-op, and how did you overcome it?

Prior to co\-op, I had little to no experience working in a corporate environment\. As much as the transition from academia to industry was rewarding, it was also a little difficult\. I had to relearn some of the skills I thought I was already proficient in, because industry standards are a little different when it comes to regulation and documentation\. Being curious, asking questions and overall being open to learn was the best way to overcome it, but it did take a while to get used to\!

### Managing the balance between academics, co\-op responsibilities and a personal life can be hard – what are your self care practices and/or how do you manage stress?

I lived on campus during my first co\-op term while working in Burnaby, and my commute time was a big adjustment for me \(1h 40m one way transit\!\)\. It forced me to rethink and reorganize my routines\. I started meal prepping to make more time for my hobbies and hanging out with friends, so that I wasn't stuck in a work\-eat\-sleep cycle\. I think it's really important to have a life and enjoy your time outside of work\. As students, it's rare to be able to go home at the end of the day and not have to study, go into the lab, do homework, etc\.\.\. so make the most of your free weekends while you're on co\-op\! During my time in Boston, I played a lot of volleyball \- tournaments, leagues and open gyms, made a lot of new friends and found a community that I could have fun with when I wasn't working\.

[Bento lunch box](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/01.jpg)

### In your opinion, how did Co\-op help your personal growth?

Co\-op helped me visualize what I wanted my career and life to look like after graduation, and made the transition from student to working full\-time a little easier\. Being able to take a "break" from studying and experience what my day\-to\-day life would look like working a job helped me become more independent, identify things I valued, and subsequently influenced what I looked for in a career after graduation when job hunting\.

> Co\-op helped me visualize what I wanted my career and life to look like after graduation, and made the transition from student to working full\-time a little easier\.

[Image](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/02%20edited.jpg)

### How do you feel Co\-op has helped your career and professional development?

I think co\-op played a big role in helping me learn what I like to do\. Prior to co\-op, I was doing a lot of pure lab work, experiments, manuscript writing\. During co\-op, I was still doing a lot of the science in the lab, but also learning more about the theory behind it, being exposed more to the business development aspect of science and biotech, planning and developing the direction of projects depending on collaborators, etc\. I learned that I enjoy and thrive working in a collaborative, project focused and cross\-functional environment, which helped me decide to pursue consulting\.

> I think co\-op played a big role in helping me learn what I like to do\. \.\.\. During co\-op, I was still doing a lot of the science in the lab, but also learning more about the theory behind it, being exposed more to the business development aspect of science and biotech, planning and developing the direction of projects depending on collaborators, etc\.

### Which supports from the Co\-op program \(workshops, practice interviews, etc\.\) did you find most helpful? Can you talk about the direct impact on your career and/or personal growth?

I definitely found the live resume review with my Co\-op Coordinator the most helpful\. It was great to get an external opinion from someone who has seen successful resumes, and I believe it was key in getting me the opportunities and interviews that I did\.

[Image](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/08.jpg)

### What advice would you offer to future Co\-op students?

Aim higher than what you think you'll reach\! Don't just apply for jobs that you are overqualified for, or hesitate on ones you think you'd really like but aren't sure of your skillset\. Co\-op is here for you to develop yourself, and you can only do that by identifying what you already can do, what you want to learn to do, and finding opportunities that balance these\.

  
Also \- SCOPE is not the only place you can find jobs\! My second co\-op at GSK was actually sourced from their company career site\. I wanted to work abroad for my second co\-op, so I definitely put in at least double the number of applications to external company sites compared to ones I also did through SCOPE\.

> Co\-op is here for you to develop yourself, and you can only do that by identifying what you already can do, what you want to learn to do, and finding opportunities that balance these\.

### What are you looking forward to after graduation?

I just graduated this May, and I'll be going back to Boston to work full\-time as a consultant with Karchem Consulting, working on lab informatics solutions and workflows\. I'm super excited to see all the friends I made while on co\-op again, and also just excited in general for the next big step in my career\.

title: Co-op and Academic Progression
content_markdown:
Students who complete **one work term during the Winter Session** of their third year may notice that their class standing remains at Year 3 in Workday and that they are not automatically promoted to Year 4\. This situation affects students in Schedule A within the following Co\-op programs: Biology, Chemistry, Earth & Ocean Sciences, Geographical Sciences, Geological Sciences, Geophysics, Microbiology, and Oceanography\. These students may encounter difficulties when registering for fourth\-year level courses in the subsequent Winter Session\. To address this issue, affected students may be eligible for a manual promotion to Year 4 class standing, provided they meet **ALL** of the following requirements:

1.  Successful completion of 72 or more credits
2.  Successful completion of at least **12** upper\-level \(300 or 400 level\) credits
3.  Successful completion of at least 50 science credits, of which **9** must be upper level \(300 or 400 level\) science credits
4.  Completed the [Laboratory Science Requirement](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/lower-level-requirements)
5.  Completed the [Communication Requirement](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/communication-requirements)

The above Rules \# 2 and 3 are modified from the [regular BSc Y4 promotion requirements](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/promotion-requirements-and-degree-progression) to account for their Co\-op participation\.  The review will be conducted in February and the Year 4 status will be used to determine registration priority and eligibility in time for Summer session\. Students who do not meet the above will *not* be promoted\.

If you have any questions, feel free to contact your Co\-op Coordinator or the [Science Advising team](https://science.ubc.ca/students/advising?t=1769018573)\.

Co\-operative education course credits cannot be used in lieu of or to complement academic course credits required by the specialization\. Refer to the [UBC Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/co-operative-education) for more information\.

title: Featured Student: Jiahe Jiang
content_markdown:
March 5, 2025

[UBC Science Co\-op Computer Science student Jiahe Jiang stands on a street in the sunlight\.](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/masthead_focal_point_sm/public/feature-images/2025-03/IMG_2377.JPG?h=e11ac020&itok=u0Fbp5dp)

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/chronicles/jiahe-jiang)

## **What is your field of study and when will you graduate?**

I'm studying for a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and expect to graduate in May 2027\.

## **Why did you choose to enroll in Co\-op?**

I chose to enroll in Co\-op, because of its significant benefits\. 

First, it provides an opportunity to apply what I’ve learned in school to real\-world work settings, enabling skill transformation and hands\-on learning\. 

Second, encouragement from friends who had positive Co\-op experiences motivated me to join\. They emphasized how Co\-op helps build both technical and soft skills, such as teamwork, communication and adaptability\.

## **Which positions did you work during Co\-op?**

My first work placement was in the Digital Information Technologies and Solutions role at Sanofi\-Pasteur\. 

During this term, I played a key role in enhancing the organization's operational efficiency and cybersecurity\. I was responsible for installing and maintaining various IQ devices, such as: Ergotron workstations, Wi\-Fi bridges and ThinClient terminals, ensuring smooth operations in the B200 building\. 

Additionally, I provided technical support for laptops and workstations and contributed to cybersecurity compliance efforts, which helped improve system reliability, enhance data security and support the organization’s overall objectives\.

## As a Computer Science major, was a career in healthcare where you initially saw yourself? What led you to apply for the Digital Information Technologies and Solutions position at Sanofi\-Pasteur?

No, healthcare was not initially the career path that I envisioned\. 

However, I've always been interested in positions within the healthcare field, because the process of vaccine development fascinates me\.

Additionally, I was drawn to the opportunity to work with cutting\-edge technologies and contribute to impactful projects that make a difference in people’s lives\.

## **Can you share your favourite experience while in Co\-op?**

One of my favorite experiences was working on the B200 project alongside my colleague Agithan to successfully deploy Aruba devices, which function as wireless hotspots to facilitate the mobility of Ergotrons\. 

Initially started in 2022, this project was reassigned to me by my supervisor, Benet\. I approached the task with careful attention to detail, seeking expert advice to resolve challenges and ensure the complete implementation of the Aruba devices \- a meaningful accomplishment for our team\.

## **What was your best achievement in Co\-op?**

My best achievement was applying my academic knowledge, especially in machine learning and algorithm optimization, to real\-world settings\. 

For instance, I enhanced the SupplyChainTrackerAutomation system while working with the FFIP team\. This experience allowed me to develop skills in database management, network security and project management, while aligning my work with organizational goals\.

### **What did you feel most challenged by and how did you overcome it?**

The first month of my Co\-op felt challenging, as I transitioned from being a student to adapting to a workplace environment in an unfamiliar industry\. 

I started with almost no knowledge about vaccine development or related applications like MES and PI\. However, my supervisor and co\-workers provided incredible support, offering guidance that helped me adapt and build the necessary knowledge and skills\.

### **How do you feel Co\-op helped your personal growth?**

Co\-op significantly contributed to my personal growth by enhancing my communication skills and ability to collaborate across departments\. I discovered that I thrive in dynamic, team\-oriented environments\. Networking opportunities during Co\-op also broadened my perspective and helped me understand the importance of professional relationships in career development\.

[Image](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/IMG_9862.JPG)

### **How do you feel Co\-op has helped your career?**

Before my Co\-op, I was passionate about software development but uncertain about which industry to pursue\. 

My experience at Sanofi exposed me to the intersection of technology and healthcare, sparking a strong interest in health\-tech\. It motivated me to explore the integration of AI in manufacturing, particularly for data analysis and workflow optimization\. 

Additionally, this experience has shaped my academic aspirations, as I am now considering this topic as a potential thesis proposal for a Master’s degree\.

### **Which supports from the Co\-op program \(workshops, practice interviews, etc\) do you feel best supported you? Can you talk about the direct impact on your career?**

The mock interview provided by my Co\-op coordinator, Keikei, was invaluable\. 

As someone with no prior interview experience, the advice and practice boosted my confidence and prepared me for applying to positions\. This support played a crucial role in helping me secure my Co\-op placement and develop professional skills\.

### **What advice would you offer to future Co\-op students?** 

I highly recommend enrolling in the Co\-op program, as it provides a unique opportunity to discover your passions and gain practical experience in a real\-world work environment\. 

Take the initiative to learn new skills, advocate for your career progression and don’t hesitate to ask for help\. Networking and consistent effort in your roles will make a significant difference in your Co\-op success\.

### **What are you looking forward to after graduation?** 

I'm excited to apply the knowledge and experience gained during my Co\-op to integrate AI into manufacturing processes, focusing on improving data analysis and optimizing workflows\. 

This aligns with my academic aspirations of pursuing a Master’s degree to further explore the use of generative AI in the healthcare industry, as well as my career objective of leveraging emerging technologies to foster innovation and enhance efficiency in industrial environments\.

**Keep in touch with Jiahe**: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jiahe-jiang-435660272/)
